help_purpose: The main tasks in Dwello, step by step.
help_buildings_1: Under «Buildings» you add a building with its address, postcode, town and year built.
help_buildings_2: Under «Apartments» or on the building’s detail page you add the apartments with apartment number, floor, area and number of rooms.
help_buildings_3: The area is the basis for distribution keys by area, so enter it accurately.
help_tenants_1: Under «Tenants» you add the tenants with their contact details and correspondence channel (letter or email).
help_tenants_2: Under «Rental contracts», «Add rental contract» guides you through the contract in five steps: tenant, apartment, contract term, rent and review. «Back» and «Next» move between the steps without losing your entries.
help_tenants_3: Only «Save rental contract» in the last step creates the rental contract. Until you save, discard the draft or sign out, your entries stay as a draft in this browser.
help_tenants_4: When a tenancy ends, enter the contract end in the rental contract. The apartment then counts as vacant again.
help_invoices_1: Under «Invoices» you add each invoice from an invoice issuer with its date, amount and building.
help_invoices_2: Every invoice belongs to a category. Only invoices in allocable categories go into the utility cost statements.
help_invoices_3: You maintain categories, distribution keys and heating profiles under «Categories», «Distribution keys» and «Heating profiles», and defaults such as the billing period under «Settings».
help_statements_1: Under «Utility cost statements», «Create statements» guides you in five steps: billing period, buildings, heating profile and management fee, preview and create.
help_statements_2: In the preview you check the costs: Dwello shares them out by distribution key and, when tenants change or an apartment is vacant, bills them by days rented. Only «Create drafts» creates the statements.
help_statements_3: The statements are then available as drafts. You can change the payment deadline and the remark; to correct wrong costs, create the statements again.
help_statements_4: Dwello does not send the statements itself. Deliver the PDF to the tenant by letter or email, then choose «Mark as sent». The payment deadline runs from that day.
help_payments_1: The «Overview» shows you overdue statements and upcoming deadlines.
help_payments_2: When a payment comes in, choose «Mark as paid» in the statement.
help_payments_3: When the payment deadline has passed, «Send reminder» issues a payment reminder or a reminder. It goes by email or as a letter, depending on the tenant’s correspondence channel.
help_payments_4: Letters appear under «Documents». After posting them, mark them as sent there.
glossary_period_text: The year for which you bill the utility costs, for example the calendar year or July to June. The invoice date decides which billing period an invoice belongs to.
glossary_advance_text: The tenant’s monthly advance for the utility costs. The utility cost statement sets it off against the actual costs.
glossary_net_rent_text: The monthly base rent, without utility costs.
glossary_additional_rent_text: Extra monthly rent, for example for a garage, parking space or cellar.
glossary_key_text: The rule by which a building’s costs are shared among the apartments, for example by area, by rooms or the same for each apartment.
glossary_profile_text: Spreads the heating costs over the twelve months in percent. If the tenant changes during the billing period, Dwello splits the heating costs by month instead of by day.
glossary_fee_text: The compensation for your management work: a percentage of each tenant’s own utility costs. Up to 3 % is usual. You choose the rate when you create the statements.
glossary_days_text: The number of days a rental contract runs in the billing period. If a tenant moves in or out during the year, they pay only the share of their days rented; the landlord bears any vacancy.
glossary_allocable_text: An allocable invoice goes into the utility cost statement, for example heating, water, caretaker or refuse. Whether an invoice is allocable follows from its category and can be changed for each invoice.
glossary_balance_text: The tenant’s share of the costs including the management fee, minus their advance payments made, rounded to 5 centimes. If the balance is positive, the tenant pays the difference (amount due); if it is negative, they get money back (refund).
glossary_deadline_text: The date by which the tenant must have paid the statement.
glossary_reminder_text: A demand for payment that you issue for a sent statement: first a payment reminder, then at most a 2nd and a 3rd reminder.
glossary_channel_text: How a tenant receives post from you: by letter (default) or by email. Email needs an email address.
glossary_status_text: Shows whether an apartment is let: let (a rental contract is running), re-let (a future rental contract has been signed), vacant or blocked. Let and re-let follow from the rental contracts; you set vacant and blocked when editing the apartment.

privacy_purpose: Which data Dwello processes and where it goes.
privacy_llm_external: Invoices are categorised by {provider} ({country}) using a language model. For this, the invoice issuer (including individuals), the description and the amount of the invoice are transmitted; if the description contains a name, it is transmitted too.
privacy_llm_local: Invoices are categorised by a language model that runs on the operator’s server; invoice data does not leave the server for this.
privacy_stored_1: Dwello stores the data needed to manage the buildings and bill the utility costs: buildings and apartments, tenants with contact details and correspondence address, rental contracts, invoices, and the statements created, payments and reminders.
privacy_stored_2: The data is kept in the PostgreSQL database of the operator of this Dwello installation.
privacy_login_1: You sign in through Google or Microsoft. Dwello receives the name, email address and profile picture of the account and uses them only to run the session and show the name in the header. Dwello never sees passwords.
privacy_third_1: Payment reminders and reminders by email are delivered through the mail service set up by the operator (its own SMTP server or Resend). The tenant’s name and email address and the content of the message are transmitted.
privacy_third_2: Fonts and symbols are loaded from Google Fonts. Google receives the browser’s IP address.
privacy_third_3: Beyond this, Dwello does not share any data with third parties.
privacy_cookies_1: Dwello sets only technically necessary cookies: a session cookie that JavaScript cannot read and a cookie that protects against forged requests (XSRF). No tracking or advertising cookies are used.
privacy_draft_notice: Dwello keeps unsaved entries in «Add rental contract» and «Create statements» as a draft in this browser until you save them, discard them or sign out. A draft may contain names and amounts; it stays on the device you are working on.
terms_purpose: What Dwello does and what the management is responsible for.
terms_operator: This Dwello installation is run by {operator}.
terms_purpose_1: Dwello helps property managers manage buildings, tenants and rental contracts and create utility cost statements under Swiss tenancy law.
terms_responsibility_1: Dwello calculates the statements from the invoices, distribution keys and rental contracts entered. The property manager remains responsible for the accuracy of the data entered and for the statements sent. Every statement should be checked before it is sent.
terms_responsibility_2: The management is responsible for informing the tenants about the processing of their data.
terms_availability_1: Operation, data backup and availability are the responsibility of the operator of this Dwello installation. There is no right to uninterrupted availability.

buildings_fuel_title: Fuel in the tank or store
buildings_fuel_intro: Only for buildings heated with oil, liquid gas, pellets or wood. What was consumed is billed: opening stock + purchases − closing stock. To do this, on the last day of each billing period, for example on 31.12., add the value in the tank or store in francs. The value of 31.12.2024 is the closing stock 2024 and the opening stock 2025. Calculate the value like this: quantity in the tank or store times the price per unit (litre, kg or stere) of the last delivery. If the tank or store holds more than the last delivery, calculate the rest at the price of the delivery before. If you only read the level at the beginning of January, still add the value as at 31.12.
